learningObjective: Compute the linear storage offset of a strided tensor element from shape, strides, and coordinate; and reason about broadcast strides.

canonicalClaims.claim: The linear storage offset of a strided tensor element is `offset = sum_i (index_i * stride_i)`. A zero stride on a dim is a legal metadata encoding for a broadcast view: all indices along that dim alias the same physical element.
conditions: Strides are in element units (or bytes, consistently).
The tensor is a read-only broadcast view (writes to zero-stride dims are typically disallowed).
nonImplications: Does not imply broadcast views are writable.
Does not imply that a broadcast avoids all copies downstream; some ops may materialize.

misconceptions.claim: Zero strides are illegal in any tensor IR.
misconceptions.whyWrong: PyTorch and MLIR memref both allow zero strides for broadcast views.

misconceptions.claim: The offset formula ignores strides and sums only coordinates.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The offset is explicitly a stride-weighted sum.

misconceptions.claim: Zero strides mean the compiler will replace them at codegen with per-element stride.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Zero strides are semantic; they intentionally alias indices to the same physical element.

misconceptions.claim: A broadcast view always allocates full physical storage `product(shape)`.
misconceptions.whyWrong: A broadcast view can share storage across dims; physical storage may be much smaller than product(logical shape).

implementationFacts: PyTorch: `expand` produces a broadcast view with zero strides on the expanded dims
MLIR memref: strided layout accepts zero strides
Writing to a broadcast view is generally disallowed or produces undefined behavior
performanceScenarios: Broadcast views avoid materializing large intermediate tensors; downstream kernels must handle strided access.
